episode_title: Ep 59 - Tribe Leader: A Tribute To My Mentor - Doug Clifton Curling
question: What were Doug Clifton Curling's seven key attributes that made him an exceptional executive leader?
transcript_excerpt: Doug Clifton Curling embodied seven unique attributes: integrity applied without exception to everyone; emotional intelligence with self-awareness and empathy that built trust without micromanagement; comfort in his own skin, refusing formality and prioritizing substance over symbol; ability to make complex problems simple and break them into logical components; understanding that people matter most and willingness to pivot when decisions led to bad outcomes; capacity to see people deeply, reading their energy and helping them move from dark to light; and knowing how to have fun, laugh at himself, and let loose with Hawaiian shirts and long hair.

episode_title: Ep 59 - Tribe Leader: A Tribute To My Mentor - Doug Clifton Curling
question: What did Doug Clifton Curling teach about redirecting employees who don't fit their current role?
transcript_excerpt: Doug taught the principle that sometimes you cannot make an orange into an apple. Instead, find out what that person does extremely well and what they love doing most—the thing they would do for free—and put them in that job in the company. If you do that, that person will add value; but if you keep trying to make the orange an apple, everyone ends up in trouble. This philosophy, applied across multiple companies, has led some former team members to rise to the executive level.

episode_title: Ep 59 - Tribe Leader: A Tribute To My Mentor - Doug Clifton Curling
question: How did Doug Clifton Curling respond when Mark Anthony Peterson wanted to fire an employee who threw a water bottle?
transcript_excerpt: Doug pulled Peterson aside and revealed context: the employee had lost his wife, was a single father raising three kids, and his identity was built on working directly with Doug. Though Doug gave Peterson full authority to fire him, he contextualized the situation with compassion. This awakening led Peterson to have a long conversation with the employee, discover what made him happy, and create a scenario where the employee could work on projects with his family around him and take on slow-fuse intellectual work. The employee's life improved significantly.

episode_title: Ep 59 - Tribe Leader: A Tribute To My Mentor - Doug Clifton Curling
question: What role did Doug Clifton Curling hold at Choice Point?
transcript_excerpt: Doug Clifton Curling served as president, chief operating officer, and board member at Choice Point, which was a spin-out of Equifax and became a publicly traded company. Mark Anthony Peterson reported to the chairman and CEO Derek Smith but spent most of his time working directly with Doug in his office.

episode_title: Ep 59 - Tribe Leader: A Tribute To My Mentor - Doug Clifton Curling
question: What water and infrastructure projects did Doug Clifton Curling pursue after Choice Point was sold?
transcript_excerpt: After Choice Point was sold and Doug became extremely well off, he traveled to Central and South America digging wells so that underserved villages could have access to clean water. This work was purely driven by his mission to serve communities without any financial necessity, demonstrating his commitment to giving back and having fun while making a real difference.
